vignette_text: A 66-year-old White female with type 2 diabetes diagnosed 3 years ago presents for diabetes follow-up. She has attempted dietary modification and intermittent exercise but has not yet started diabetes medication because she has been hesitant about both gastrointestinal side effects and injectable therapies. Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea treated with CPAP, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease identified on ultrasound. She reports gradual weight gain over the past 5 years and increasing frustration with difficulty losing weight despite lifestyle efforts. She denies polyuria, polydipsia, blurry vision, neuropathy symptoms, or hypoglycemia. She has never been hospitalized for diabetes-related complications. On examination, BMI is 39 kg/m2, blood pressure 136/82 mmHg, and waist circumference is 116 cm. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable. Labs: HbA1c 7.9%, fasting glucose 168 mg/dL, eGFR 72 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 22 mg/g, AST 30 U/L, ALT 38 U/L, total cholesterol 208 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, LDL 118 mg/dL, triglycerides 228 mg/dL. She is a never smoker. Current medications include valsartan, hydrochlorothiazide, rosuvastatin, and nightly CPAP use. She expresses strong interest in weight loss and tighter glycemic control but is reluctant to start injections and worries about medication cost.
